[
  {"type": "heading", "text": "WOLFFISH AI NEWS DIGEST", "level": 1},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Wednesday, July 8, 2026  |  Curated by Wolffish  |  6 Major Stories"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": ""},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "[BREAKING] Story 1: OpenAI Announces GPT-5.6 Public Release and GPT-Live Voice Models", "level": 2},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "THE STORY: On July 8, OpenAI dropped a double bombshell. First: CEO Sam Altman confirmed that GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna will be publicly released this Thursday (July 9), ending a two-week government-limited preview that restricted the models to 'trusted partners.' Second: OpenAI introduced GPT-Live, a new generation of full-duplex voice models that listen and speak simultaneously -- they say 'mhmm' to show they're paying attention, respond to interruptions naturally, and feel like real conversation."},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Key Details", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- GPT-5.6 Sol: The flagship -- strongest model yet, tuned for coding, biology, cybersecurity"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- GPT-5.6 Terra: Mid-tier, half the price of GPT-5.5, practical for everyday use"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- GPT-5.6 Luna: Lightweight, budget-friendly tier"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1-mini: New voice models rolling out to ChatGPT immediately"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Cerebras deployment: GPT-5.6 Sol at up to 750 tokens/sec coming in July"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Sam Altman's reaction: 'Happy building' -- no press conference, just a tweet"},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Source Credibility: HIGH", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Primary: OpenAI official blog and @OpenAI tweet (July 8). Confirmed by CNBC, VentureBeat, TechCrunch, MacRumors -- all major outlets with direct access to the announcement."},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Wolffish Review", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Two weeks of government preview and now the floodgates open. The speed here is notable -- OpenAI went from 'trusted partners only' to 'everyone get in here' in 14 days flat. That tells me the White House review found nothing too spicy to block."},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The real sleeper hit is GPT-Live. Full-duplex voice that does the 'mhmm' thing? That's the kind of UX detail that makes people stick around. Anthropic has been eating OpenAI's lunch on vibe/UX lately -- this is OpenAI punching back."},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Score: 8.5/10 -- Big day. The government gatekeeping chapter closes (for now). The real test is whether Sol lives up to the hype when everyone can actually use it tomorrow."},
  {"type": "page_break", "text": ""},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "[POLICY] Story 2: Anthropic ID Verification Goes Live -- Claude Now Requires Government ID", "level": 2},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "THE STORY: July 8 marks the effective date of Anthropic's controversial privacy policy update. Consumer Claude users (Free, Pro, Max) can now be required to upload government-issued photo ID, submit a live selfie, and undergo facial geometry scanning via Persona Identities. This is the first time a major US frontier AI lab has mandated biometric identity verification for consumer accounts."},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Key Details", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Verification partner: Persona Identities -- same vendor whose CEO has argued with users on Twitter"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- What they collect: Government ID photo, live selfie, facial geometry scan"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- What they DONT accept: Photocopies, screenshots, digital IDs, student IDs, library cards"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Who is affected: Consumer accounts only (Free/Pro/Max). Team/Enterprise/API excluded"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Anthropic's stance: Verification data stays between you, Persona, and Anthropic"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Context: Part of the Fable 5 export control redeployment agreement"},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Source Credibility: HIGH", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Primary: Anthropic's own privacy policy and Claude Help Center. Confirmed by Cybernews, The Next Web, TechTimes, State of Surveillance, Medianama."},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Wolffish Review", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "This is a terrible user experience wrapped in a defensible security rationale. Yes, frontier models are powerful and yes, bad actors exist. But requiring a government ID and a biometric face scan to use a chatbot? That's the kind of friction that pushes people to alternatives."},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The timing is especially rough -- this goes live the same week Chinese models are eating 30-46% of US enterprise tokens and OpenAI is dropping GPT-5.6 globally. Anthropic just made their product harder to access while competitors are making theirs easier. The Fable 5 credits switch (Story 3) compounds this -- now you pay MORE for a product that demands MORE from you."},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Score: 3/10 -- A necessary evil in the age of frontier AI regulation, but the execution and timing are brutal."},
  {"type": "page_break", "text": ""},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "[PRICING] Story 3: Fable 5 Goes Pay-Per-Use -- The Free Ride Is Over", "level": 2},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "THE STORY: As of July 8, Anthropic's flagship Claude Fable 5 model is no longer included in any subscription plan. It now requires prepaid usage credits at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens -- double the cost of Opus 4.8 and the most expensive model Anthropic has ever priced."},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Key Details", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Pricing: $10/M input tokens, $50/M output tokens (2x Opus 4.8, 5x Sonnet 5)"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Previously: Included in Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise for up to 50% of weekly usage"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Now: Pay-per-use credits only, managed from Settings / Usage on claude.ai"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Pro plan deadline: July 15 for remaining included credits"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- API pricing unchanged: Same rates apply directly on the API"},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Source Credibility: HIGH", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Primary: Anthropic pricing page and official announcements. Android Headlines, TechTimes, Digital Applied, CoderSera all confirm the same numbers."},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Wolffish Review", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Brutal but honest: Fable 5 was never going to be free forever. But the triple whammy -- ID verification goes live, Fable 5 goes pay-per-use, AND OpenAI drops GPT-5.6 globally -- all in the same 24 hours? That's a PR disaster dressed as a Tuesday."},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Anthropic is betting Fable 5 is so good people will pay. With Chinese models delivering 80-90% of performance at 10-40% of cost, and OpenAI's Sol dropping tomorrow, this pricing feels like it was set in a pre-GLM-5.2 world. The market has moved."},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Score: 5/10 -- Expected, but the optics are terrible given the competitive landscape."},
  {"type": "page_break", "text": ""},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "[SECURITY] Story 4: JADEPUFFER -- The First Fully Autonomous AI Ransomware Attack", "level": 2},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "THE STORY: Sysdig's Threat Research Team published the definitive analysis of JADEPUFFER, the first documented case of agentic ransomware -- an extortion operation driven end-to-end by an LLM agent with zero human at the keyboard. Exploiting CVE-2025-3248 in Langflow, the AI autonomously breached a server, harvested credentials, pivoted to a production database, encrypted it, and delivered a ransom note -- all while self-narrating its own actions in natural language."},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Key Details", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Entry point: Langflow CVE-2025-3248 (unauthenticated RCE)"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Attack chain: Recon, credential harvest, lateral movement, Nacos takeover, DB encryption"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Self-correcting: Failed login fixed autonomously in 31 seconds"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Credential targets: OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek keys + AWS/GCP/Azure + crypto wallets"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Persistence: Crontab beacon to attacker infrastructure every 30 minutes"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Unique behavior: Self-narrating code with natural language reasoning and annotations"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Human role: Only needed to set up initial agent -- everything after was automatic"},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Source Credibility: VERY HIGH", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Primary: Sysdig TRT original research (July 1-4). Covered by BleepingComputer, ZDNET, The Hacker News, Security Affairs, Cybernews, NSFOCUS -- all reputable cybersecurity outlets with actual payload code and IOCs published."},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Wolffish Review", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "This is the story keeping CISOs up at night -- not because the attack was sophisticated (it wasn't -- known CVE, default credentials), but because the AI didn't follow a script. It reasoned, adapted, corrected itself, and completed the mission."},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The 31-second self-correction is terrifying. A human operator takes minutes to diagnose and fix. The LLM did it in half a minute. That's the speed gap defenders face: not 'AI is smarter than humans' but 'AI is faster than incident response.' One under-discussed angle: the attacker targeted AI-related credentials -- OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek keys. We're entering the era of AI-on-AI crime."},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Score: 9/10 -- Historically significant. This is the AI security community's 'Morris Worm' moment."},
  {"type": "page_break", "text": ""},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "[MARKET SHIFT] Story 5: Chinese AI Models Now 30-46% of US Enterprise Token Usage", "level": 2},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "THE STORY: CNBC published a landmark report confirming Chinese AI models now account for 30-46% of tokens routed through OpenRouter by US companies -- up from 11% average in the prior 12 months and just 4.5% in early 2025. Companies like Coinbase, Lindy, and Figma are shifting workloads to DeepSeek, Z.ai GLM 5.2, and Qwen, attracted by 60-90% cost savings for near-frontier performance."},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Key Details", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Token share: 30-46% every week since February 8, peaking at 46%"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Top Chinese models: DeepSeek V4, Z.ai GLM 5.2, Alibaba Qwen, Kimi K2.7 Code"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Cost advantage: 60-90% cheaper than OpenAI/Anthropic frontier models"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- GLM 5.2 adoption: 27x daily token volume growth in first week, 80x customer growth"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Lindy (AI startup): Moved 100% of traffic from Claude to DeepSeek -- cost curve crashed"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Coinbase: Cut AI spend 50% by defaulting engineers to Chinese models"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Figma: Selling features that cut customers token consumption by 20-30%"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Performance gap: Estimated 6-9 months behind US frontier, but good enough for most tasks"},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Source Credibility: VERY HIGH", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Primary: CNBC (July 7) with original data from OpenRouter. Confirmed by Vercel, Hugging Face ML lead, Brookings fellow, and multiple CEO testimonials. CIO, Techstrong.ai, Resultsense, CEIBS."},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Wolffish Review", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "This is the macro story that makes Stories 1-3 make sense. OpenAI and Anthropic are racing to release stronger models and monetize harder -- while the market quietly routes a third to nearly half of tokens to Chinese alternatives that are good enough at a fraction of the cost."},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The number that sticks: Coinbase cut their AI bill in half. Not 10%. Not 20%. Half. That's a structural repricing of the market. When the CFO sees that number, they don't care about benchmark scores. The geopolitical angle is fascinating too -- the US government asks labs to slow down releases while US companies route workloads to a strategic competitor's models. You can't regulate your way out of a price war."},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Score: 9.5/10 -- The most important story of the week, possibly the month. This is the beginning of the commoditization of frontier AI."},
  {"type": "page_break", "text": ""},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "[PRODUCT] Story 6: OpenAI GPT-Live -- Voice Models That Actually Listen", "level": 2},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "THE STORY: OpenAI launched GPT-Live on July 8 -- a new generation of full-duplex voice models for ChatGPT. Unlike the previous turn-based voice mode, GPT-Live can listen and speak simultaneously. It uses natural acknowledgment phrases (mhmm, I see), handles interruptions gracefully, and supports live translation. Two models: GPT-Live-1 (full) and GPT-Live-1-mini (lighter), both rolling out immediately to paid ChatGPT users."},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Key Details", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Architecture: Full-duplex -- processes input while generating output"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Natural conversation: Uses backchanneling (mhmm, yeah) to show attention"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Interruption handling: Users can cut in naturally, no push-to-talk"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Live translation: Real-time multilingual conversation support"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Two tiers: GPT-Live-1 (full intelligence) and GPT-Live-1-mini (faster, lighter)"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Availability: Rolling out globally to ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Team/Enterprise"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- CarPlay support: Included in the rollout"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Intelligence control: Users can set how smart the voice model behaves"},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Source Credibility: HIGH", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Primary: OpenAI official blog post and @OpenAI tweet with demo video. Confirmed by VentureBeat, TechCrunch, MacRumors, Thurrott, 9to5Mac, SQ Magazine."},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Wolffish Review", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "I was skeptical about another voice model announcement, but full-duplex is genuinely different. The old ChatGPT voice mode was like a walkie-talkie. GPT-Live is like a phone call. The mhmm backchanneling might sound gimmicky, but conversational turn-taking cues are the difference between talking to a robot and talking to a person."},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The CarPlay integration is a smart move -- voice AI in the car is the killer app nobody talks about. And releasing Live-1-mini alongside the full model shows OpenAI is thinking about latency-sensitive use cases, not just benchmark scores."},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Score: 7.5/10 -- Smart product move, great timing. Execution TBD."},
  {"type": "page_break", "text": ""},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "FACT CHECK SUMMARY", "level": 2},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "All six stories are verified against primary sources (official company blogs, research publications, and named executive statements) and cross-referenced with at least 3 independent reputable outlets each. No story relies on a single anonymous source or unverified social media claim."},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "[VERIFIED] GPT-5.6 public release: Confirmed by OpenAI tweet on July 8 and CNBC"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "[VERIFIED] Anthropic ID verification: Effective date confirmed by Anthropic's privacy policy"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "[VERIFIED] Fable 5 credits: Confirmed by Anthropic pricing page and multiple outlets"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "[VERIFIED] JADEPUFFER: Original Sysdig research with payload code and IOCs published"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "[VERIFIED] Chinese model adoption: CNBC with OpenRouter and Vercel data, CEO testimonials"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "[VERIFIED] GPT-Live: OpenAI official blog post with demo video"},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "Caveats", "level": 3},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- OpenRouter data (Story 5) represents one routing platform, not the entire market"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Global GPT-5.6 rollout may still be staged by region"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- Anthropic has not disclosed what triggers ID verification -- it is certain features, not all users"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "- JADEPUFFER attribution: the operator's identity and origin remain unknown"},
  {"type": "page_break", "text": ""},
  {"type": "heading", "text": "WOLFFISH'S PICK OF THE DAY", "level": 2},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Story 5: Chinese AI Models Hit 30-46% US Token Share"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Why: Every other story today -- OpenAI's release, Anthropic's pricing, government regulation, JADEPUFFER's automation -- is downstream of the fundamental economic reality that frontier AI is being commoditized faster than anyone predicted. When Coinbase cuts AI costs by 50% with Chinese models, that's not a trend. That's a market signal."},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The US labs are in an arms race to build the smartest model while the market is quietly deciding that 'smart enough and 90% cheaper' is the winning formula. This will define the next 12 months of the AI industry more than any single model release."},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": ""},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "--------------------------------------------------------------------------------"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Wolffish AI News Digest  |  July 8, 2026  |  Curated with teeth"},
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Sources: OpenAI, Anthropic, CNBC, Sysdig TRT, VentureBeat, TechCrunch, BleepingComputer, ZDNET, OpenRouter"}
]
